title: Stargazer inference economics & console walkthrough
summary: Intro + console demo focused on per-route economics. Showed Route view, token-level cost breakdown, latency P95/P99, and Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization). Discussed hosted vs dedicated for PHI workflows, VPC/KMS requirements, SOC2 and SSO. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot: Redwood to provide security pack, pricing for 6-month reserved capacity trial, and a benchmarking plan for Stargazer's longest-context route.
topics: Per-route cost attribution and token breakdown
Latency SLOs: P95 vs P99 and tail behavior
Batching, KV/prefix caching, and Optimize recommendations
Hosted API vs Dedicated (reserved capacity) for PHI workloads
Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
Pilot and benchmark plan for long-context routing

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20 14:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Oliver Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Nair (CTO - Stargazer), Carlos Mendes (Lead ML Eng - Stargazer), Amrita Rao (PM - Stargazer)

Summary: quick walkthrough of the Redwood Console focusing on per-route economics, and a discussion about whether Stargazer should run PHI processing on hosted or go dedicated / VPC. Demonstrated Optimize suggestions and cost/latency tradeoffs.

00:00 Oliver (AE): okay, thanks everyone for joining, we've got about an hour, going to show the console route economics page and a couple things from Optimize. Maya will cover the deep bits.
00:18 Priya: thanks, yeah we just want to see the per-route cost because our discharge-summary endpoint spiked costs last month and procurement is asking why.
00:32 Maya (SE): awesome, we'll start on the Routes overview — this is the 'Route list' view, shows top routes by spend, rps, and p95 latency. Note the heatmap on the right highlights long context usage which often correlates with token cost.
00:48 Carlos: is that token cost broken down per system vs user tokens? we mix user-provided notes and system prompt.
01:05 Maya: yes, the breakdown shows user vs system vs embeddings if used; cost column is normalized to USD per 1k tokens for the current billing profile, and you can toggle to show raw token counts. sometimes the transcription has small label errors so the UI might show 'systemt' in older exports.
01:28 Amrita: I like the trend line — can you show why discharge-summary is expensive?
01:35 Maya: sure, clicking into the route — Route detail page — you'll see per-invocation distribution: median tokens, 75th, 95th, and top tail. For your discharge-summary route we see a long tail at 99th percentile, which is likely the long patient history included in some requests.
01:55 Oliver: quick note on terminology — we use prefix/KV cache; prefix cache caches the initial prompt fragments and KV cache is for decoder state across streaming? there was a doc that conflated them, so sorry if terms swapped in the past.
02:12 Carlos: can you explain how caching affects cost?
02:18 Maya: caching reduces the tokens the model sees again — prefix cache will avoid re-sending static boilerplate. For repeated templates it drops tokens billed and improves latency. Also Optimize suggests cache TTLs per route.
02:35 Priya: our compliance team is strict — any caching of PHI is a red flag. How is that handled?
02:43 Maya: valid concern. cache entries can be configured to encrypt with customer KMS keys and set tight TTLs, or you can disable prefix caching for PHI routes. For most customers we recommend dedicated deployment if PHI retention is a concern.
03:05 Amrita: can you show the cost per 1M tokens side-by-side?
03:12 Maya: yep — here's the 'Economics panel' next to the route — shows effective unit cost after batching and cache. You'll also see a column for 'Optimize suggestions' which ranks potential savings by percentage; for discharge-summary it suggests increasing batch window from 5ms to 25ms which could reduce unit cost ~18% at current traffic mix.
03:42 Carlos: that batching suggestion — does it increase latency tail? we can't impact p99 for clinical flows.
03:50 Maya: it's workload dependent. Optimize simulates impact: it estimates p95 and p99 changes using your traffic distribution. For high priority routes you can pin latency SLOs; Optimize will only recommend changes that keep p99 within your target. In our simulation for this route p95 improved and p99 increased by 30ms on edge cases — we can show the breakdown.
04:20 Priya: what's the difference if we move to Dedicated? are we paying more?
04:28 Oliver: dedicated (reserved capacity) gives predictable throughput and you avoid per-token variability; unit cost often drops with a commit but you trade flexibility. For very high-consumption routes with tight SLOs and PHI, Dedicated behind a VPC is common. We can model a 6-month reserved capacity to show break-even.
04:48 Carlos: do you support private deployments on-prem?
04:52 Maya: yes, we have Private (VPC/on-prem) packages. On-prem is an option but involves extra ops work. For most regulated customers we do a VPC-private control plane + customer-managed network.
05:08 Amrita: what about KMS and key ownership?
05:12 Maya: you can bring your own keys (BYOK) via KMS/HSM integrations. Audit logs capture any key usage for inference sessions.
05:25 Priya: SOC2 and SSO — procurement wants those.
05:28 Oliver: we'll send the SOC2 Type II report and our SSO/SAML integration docs. Maya will include details on audit log retention and RBAC controls.
05:45 Maya: switching to the console, showing the "Route timeline" — time-series of spend with correlated changes to model version, quantization profile, and rollout percentage. This helps surface if a spike is due to a model change or a prompt template update.
06:12 Carlos: that model-change correlation is neat. can you show a CSV export? our finance team wants raw numbers.
06:19 Maya: export is available per-route, includes tokens, cost, average latency buckets, and the model variant used. we also provide a downloadable benchmark spreadsheet if you want a pre-built view.
06:35 Priya: can you run the benchmark against our sample traces or do we need to upload them?
06:42 Oliver: send us a sanitized trace set (or we can run on-site with a data handling agreement). For initial bench we usually accept redacted traces. Carlos, you mentioned 10 example long-context requests?
06:55 Carlos: yes I'll upload them to the secure share.
07:02 Maya: thanks; I'll outline the benchmark plan: baseline with hosted model, then simulate dedicated pool with same model to estimate p95/p99 and cost per token. We'll also try quantized variants to show cost tradeoffs.
07:20 Amrita: can Redwood's Optimize recommend quantization levels? we worry about quality regressions for clinical language.
07:28 Maya: Optimize includes quality monitoring — it ties regressions back to prompt sets and provides an eval harness. We won't auto-replace a model in production without your sign-off; Optimize gives recommended quant levels and shows expected ROUGE/BLEU-like deltas for generated text. For clinical, we'd run a focused eval on labeled prompts.
07:53 Priya: fine, we'll need that evaluation evidence for compliance.
08:00 Oliver: switching to the "Per-team attribution" view — shows tags you can attach to routes (eg: discharge-team, billing-api) and then we show cost split across org units and projects. Good for chargeback to product orgs.
08:20 Carlos: can tags be injected via API so our gateway adds them automatically?
08:25 Maya: yes, tags can be set via the Redwood SDK or by middleware at the proxy layer. The console will roll-up by tag.
08:36 Amrita: when you talk about streaming, do you charge per partial chunk?
08:40 Maya: billing is still token-based; streaming just changes latency perception. We show streaming token delta separately in the console so you can see if streaming overhead is material.
08:55 Priya: okay but one operational risk is misattribution if internal monitoring changes. how accurate is the per-route attribution?
09:02 Maya: we do best-effort mapping by route identifier and model variant; for gateways we recommend adding a unique route id header. There's also a 'fallback mapping' page where you can resolve ambiguous traces. There will be edge cases (e.g., async fanout) that need instrumentation.
09:26 Carlos: can you demo a live drill into the biggest spike?
09:30 Maya: sure — pulling last 30-day view, filter to discharge-summary, zoom into Oct 2 spike — see a correlated model rollout and a context length increase. The "Query inspector" shows an anonymized example invocation where the user included a 12k token history. That explains the spike.
09:55 Priya: that's exactly our issue. So what's the short-term mitigation?
10:00 Maya: short-term you can block long requests at the gateway, or enforce context trimming; Optimize suggests a prompt rewriting policy to remove redundant history. Medium-term is caching common boilerplate and batching tweaks.
10:18 Carlos: if we block long requests, do you surface errors in the console?
10:22 Maya: yes, blocked requests show up as policy rejections with metrics and sample traces. You can configure alerts when tail tokens exceed thresholds.
10:34 Amrita: can we set up canary rollouts per route? sometimes we want 10% test traffic on new quantized model.
10:40 Maya: absolutely — the rollout panel lets you set % and a rollback policy tied to quality or latency regressions. If quality drops per your eval set, it can auto-roll back.
11:00 Priya: what's the typical turnaround to enable a VPC-private deployment?
11:06 Oliver: depends on region and contract; typical is 4-8 weeks after contract and network peering are agreed. For on-prem it's longer.
11:15 Carlos: latency targets — can you provide p99 < 300ms for small-context completions?
11:22 Maya: with appropriate dedicated capacity and the right model we can hit that, but p99 is sensitive to sequence length. We'll include a latency SLO modeling in the benchmark.
11:38 Amrita: procurement will ask about cost smoothing. can we get invoicing alignment for reserved capacity?
11:43 Oliver: yes we have monthly invoicing for reserved contracts and can map usage to invoices in the billing exports.
11:52 Priya: curious — who else you work with in healthcare? any references?
11:56 Oliver: we have a couple of health customers we can request approval to share references; I'll check and include that in the security pack.
12:08 Maya: quick demo of the Optimize suggestions pane — it shows top n routes by potential savings, estimated delta in USD and expected impact to p95/p99, and confidence score. For discharge-summary Optimize flags cache potential, batch window, and a quantization candidate (low confidence due to clinical vocabulary).
12:36 Carlos: that confidence score — how is it computed?
12:40 Maya: based on historical evals, prompt stability, and similarity to our benchmark corpus; we bake in a quality-sensitivity factor for domains like medical.
12:52 Priya: ok good. I think we have a plan.
12:57 Oliver: recap: Redwood will send SOC2 and KMS notes, pricing for a 6-month reserved trial, and a benchmark plan. Stargazer will share traces and internal stakeholders. We'll set up a SE onboarding call next week.
13:15 Amrita: thanks, we'll review and get back on the pilot scope.
13:22 Maya: any last technical Qs?
13:26 Carlos: one small thing — does the console surface model quantization level in the route timeline? we need to see which invocations used q4_0 vs q8_0.
13:34 Maya: yes, model variant shows in the timeline and export; you'll see quant tag in the CSV.
13:44 Priya: thanks everyone.
13:47 Oliver: thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings ("systemt"), speaker handoffs sometimes labeled generically in the raw export. Some timestamps are rounded.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
